# EventConductor

> Event-driven workflow / saga orchestration engine for Java/Spring. Describe a business process as a workflow definition (YAML or JSON) made of steps; the engine drives the state machine, retries, timeouts and compensation, and delegates business logic to stateless workers or built-in steps (HTTP_CALL, LLM_CALL, PUBLISH_EVENT). Scales from a single in-process JVM (no Kafka, no DB) to a multi-pod cluster (Kafka + PostgreSQL) with no change to business code.

Two properties select the topology: `workflow.mode` (`embedded` | `kafka`, default `embedded`) and `workflow.persistence` (`memory` | `jpa`, default `memory`). Artifacts are on Maven Central under `io.mateu.workflow` (`workflow-engine`, `workflow-test`, `workflow-maven-plugin`, `forms-engine`, `rule-engine`, `rule-runtime`, `worker-embedded`, `worker-kafka`, `worker-http`, `worker-llm`, `inbound-events-kafka`, …), one version for all. Secure by default: the REST API needs an API key or Spring Security, the consoles and MCP need Spring Security (`workflow.message-api.allow-anonymous=true` for local development only).

## AI reference files

- [Compact reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/main/doc/public/eventconductor-ai-compact.md): setup, DSL rules, decision guide, step types, workers, testing, REST/MCP, security, gotchas. Fits a context window; use for day-to-day generation.
- [Full reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/main/doc/public/eventconductor-ai-full.md): everything — every step and field, deployment modes, Kafka, Java API, operations, security, upgrade notes 2.27 → 2.33.
- [Claude Code skills](https://github.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/tree/main/.claude/skills): `eventconductor` (definitions, patterns, testing, workers, operations, security, gotchas), `eventconductor-scaffold` (new project), `eventconductor-run` (run and verify). Copy `.claude/skills/eventconductor*` into your project's `.claude/skills/`.
- [Validated patterns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/main/.claude/skills/eventconductor/reference/patterns.md): saga with timer, human approval, HTTP integration, event-triggered flow, request/response, forEach fan-out, polling, LLM call, updates, flow control, child process, sensitive data. Every example is checked by the build against the schema and the engine.
- [Workflow definition JSON Schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/main/modules/workflow-engine/src/main/resources/workflow-definition-schema.json): editor autocomplete and validation (also `events-schema.json`, `cron-schema.json`).
- [OpenAPI of /workflow/api](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/main/doc/public/openapi/eventconductor-api.yaml).

## Key rules for generating definitions

- Every step has `id`, `type` and `name`; unknown keys are refused by the schema.
- At most one `START`; every other step needs a precondition (`preconditionStepId`, `preconditionStepIds`, or `preconditions: [{stepId, expression, onFalse}]`) — except compensation steps and a `WAIT_FOR_MESSAGE` that begins a flow.
- Steps run by data flow, never array order; no precondition cycles (use `forEach`, `repeat`, `loopBack`).
- One `END`; converge FORK branches with an AND `JOIN`, CHOICE branches with `joinType: XOR`.
- Saga: `compensable: true` + `compensationStepId`; compensation steps have no preconditions.
- Ask-and-wait: `awaitReply` on the HTTP_CALL / PUBLISH_EVENT, not a WAIT_FOR_MESSAGE after it.
- No credentials in definitions: HTTP via `workflow.http.connections` / `workflow.http.auth.<name>` / `${secret:NAME}`, LLM keys in `workflow.llm.connections`.
- Validate with `mvn eventconductor:validate`; test with `@EventConductorTest` (`io.mateu.workflow:workflow-test`).
